subject: Re: Bytedance <> Encord - training data
text:
Hi Matt,

I have some points that need clarification and  discussion as follows:
1. Please find the attached data spec for your reference. We categorize data into three tiers: L1 raw data, L2 hand tracking, and L3 text annotation. The spec is only for reference, as all data we purchased previously was off-the-shelf data.
2. In terms of raw data, there are three variants: ego-head only, ego + wrist cameras, ego + wrist + exo third-person view. Could you provide separate pricing and weekly production capacity for each type?
3. On top of raw data, hand tracking and text annotation services will be required. Please quote the respective fees for these two annotation types. Also, could you share the accuracy metrics of your hand tracking, the granularity level of your text annotations, and provide relevant samples for our review?
4. The samples you provided earlier generally meet our baseline requirements, yet there remain several critical issues. For one thing, the MANO model was not configured with the camera’s actual intrinsic parameters. In addition, the third-person view cameras were placed too far from the subjects in the footage.
5. Regarding environments, I’d like to know the price differences between them. If third-person view footage can be captured in household scenes, I believe it will meet our requirements.

[image]

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
Meng

Leo -

That said, last week before I met Adithya, I had sent a few questions (I will paste below here again). Some Adi and I discussed, some needs answers from Encord's side. I hope this made it to you as you mentioned that Adi is on vacation this week.

these are the questions that had come up during our internal review.

  *   Scope of “1M Frames”: Clarify what is specifically covered under the “1 million frames” definition.

  *   Tiering for Generalists: Explore whether tiered structures can be introduced to account for varying task complexity, including differentiated rates for more advanced work to reduce churn.
  *   Pricing Flexibility at Scale: Given the expected volume of annotation needs, assess opportunities for additional pricing concessions.
  *   Seat Model Flexibility: Determine how flexible Encord’s seat model is, particularly for ad hoc participation, and compare to models like Labelbox that offer unlimited seats for greater workflow flexibility.

When can we have answers for this?

--
Santosh Balasubramanian

Dear Nick,

Thank you very much for our productive exploratory discussion yesterday. It was great learning more about Encord’s capabilities in teleoperation and annotation workflows.

As agreed, we would like to transition our discussions to a confidential stage and proceed with a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA). Please find attached our proposed NDA draft from the Bosch side: NDA_2026-06-19_Robot_Data_Encord.pdf.

We kindly ask you to review this draft. Please note that this draft is based on our standard, pre-approved terms. Any major changes or substantial revisions will require us to involve our legal department, which will unfortunately lead to process-related delays in our collaboration. We hope we can proceed with this draft as smoothly as possible.

To prepare the formal signature process and complete our standard export control and compliance checks, could you please provide us with the following details?

Information Required:

  *   DocuSign Signatory:  Name and email address of the authorized person who will sign the NDA on your side.
  *   Military & Defense Sector:     Whether Encord is active as a business partner in the military or defense sector (relevant for export control purposes).
  *   ECCN (Export Control):             The Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) for your technology or software, if available.
  *   Cryptography:              Whether your technology or software uses cryptography or encryption.

Thank you for your support. We look forward to receiving your feedback and continuing our collaboration.
